title: Solvable Game
body_html:
Solvable Game

A game is solvable if the set $S^\infty$ of rationalizable outcomes is reduced to a singleton: $$ S^\infty=\{s^*\}. $$ This captures games whose common-rationality elimination process predicts a unique profile.

References

  • [MFoGT, Def. 4.4.3] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MathFoundationsGameTheory.pdf. A game is solvable if the rationalizable outcome set is a singleton.
  • [MFoGT, Section 1.3.3] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MathFoundationsGameTheory.pdf. Earlier use of solvability for iterated elimination.
